publicationRule: Only opportunities where at least one Toppenish High School student may qualify. Geographic reach may be Toppenish, Yakima County/Valley, Washington, the Pacific Northwest, or national. Confirmed opportunities use current sponsor information. Long-running expected opportunities may use 2025–26 school-year data or the most recent official cycle for planning when they include a prior deadline, a sponsor link, a last-checked date, and an explicit warning that deadlines, awards, eligibility, and program availability are not guaranteed. This list is maintained manually; nightly checks preserve records and flag source changes for review.

scholarships.name: Mollie Davis Scholarship
scholarships.award: Up to $10,000/year for a bachelor's degree or $4,500/year for an associate degree
scholarships.eligibility: U.S. citizens who reside in Yakima County and will pursue a first associate or bachelor's degree full time.
scholarships.expectedWindow: 2027 application opens December 1, 2026
scholarships.whyFit: Toppenish residents qualify because Toppenish is in Yakima County. This is the countywide Mollie Davis program—not Yakima Rotary's school-limited Academic or Vocational scholarships.

scholarships.name: YVC Vineyard & Winery Technology Scholarship
scholarships.organization: Yakima Valley College Vineyard & Winery Technology Program
scholarships.eligibility: New or returning part-time or full-time YVC students pursuing a degree or certificate in Vineyard Technology or Winery Technology.
scholarships.expectedWindow: Open now — applications are accepted every quarter.
scholarships.whyFit: A direct local option for Toppenish students entering YVC's vineyard or winery technology programs; the official page says awards are available every quarter.

scholarships.name: Live Your Dream Award
scholarships.award: Local awards vary; recipients can receive up to $16,000 across award levels
scholarships.eligibility: Women who provide the primary financial support for themselves and dependents, are enrolled in or accepted to an undergraduate or vocational program, and do not hold or pursue a graduate degree.
scholarships.expectedWindow: Open now — applications are accepted August 1–November 15.
scholarships.whyFit: Toppenish students are not excluded, but this is only for a student who supports dependents. It should be shared privately with students who may fit.

scholarships.name: Horse Heaven Hills Wine Growers Scholarship
scholarships.eligibility: Students with a 3.0+ GPA studying viticulture, enology, wine business, or wine-related hospitality; preference goes to Yakima, Benton, or Klickitat County residents whose parent works in Washington's wine industry.
scholarships.expectedWindow: The 2026 application closed April 14; the 2027 date has not been released and may change.
scholarships.whyFit: Toppenish is in Yakima County, one of the sponsor's preferred counties. The strongest match is a student with a parent employed in Washington's wine industry.

scholarships.name: Walter Clore Scholarship
scholarships.eligibility: Students with a 3.0+ GPA studying a wine- or viticulture-related field at a Washington college, university, community college, or technical school.
scholarships.expectedWindow: The 2026 application closed April 14; the 2027 date has not been released and may change.
scholarships.whyFit: Toppenish students can apply if their planned program is wine- or viticulture-related and they meet the sponsor's academic and enrollment rules.

scholarships.name: George & Susan Carter Scholarship
scholarships.award: $1,000 per year, renewable for up to four years
scholarships.eligibility: Students with a 3.4+ high school GPA pursuing viticulture, enology, or related food-science study; financial need is preferred.
scholarships.expectedWindow: The 2026 application closed April 14; the 2027 date has not been released and may change.
scholarships.whyFit: Toppenish students are geographically eligible when pursuing an approved wine-related program and meeting the sponsor's GPA and enrollment rules.

scholarships.name: Dairy Strong Scholarship
scholarships.award: One $5,000 award and two $1,500 awards in the 2026 cycle
scholarships.eligibility: Washington dairy employees, immediate family of a dairy employee or owner, or students active in a dairy club or education program; any major and accredited university, trade school, or community college can qualify.
scholarships.expectedWindow: The 2026 application ran February 20–June 1; the 2027 date has not been released and may change.
scholarships.whyFit: Toppenish students can qualify through their own or an immediate family member's work at a Washington dairy, or through an eligible dairy education program.

scholarships.name: Coca-Cola Scholars Program Scholarship
scholarships.eligibility: Current Class of 2027 seniors who plan to attend an accredited U.S. college, have a 3.0+ GPA, and meet federal-aid citizenship/residency categories. Strong leadership and service record expected.
scholarships.expectedWindow: Open now; closes 5 p.m. Eastern / 2 p.m. Pacific
scholarships.whyFit: Toppenish High School qualifies geographically because the program accepts students attending high school in any U.S. state. Individual applicants must also meet the listed citizenship/residency, 3.0 GPA, graduation-year, college-plan, and Coca-Cola family-employment rules.

scholarships.name: Washington State Opportunity Scholarship — Career & Technical
scholarships.eligibility: Washington residents within the income limit who will earn a high school credential by June, complete FAFSA or WASFA, and pursue an eligible associate degree, certificate, or apprenticeship. Applicants cannot already hold a bachelor's degree or plan to move directly into one after the funded program.
scholarships.expectedWindow: Winter–spring 2026–27 cycle opens September 29
scholarships.whyFit: Toppenish students qualify geographically as Washington residents; Yakima County also meets the Rural Jobs Initiative county rule. Each student still needs an eligible program and must meet income, financial-aid, and education-plan requirements.

scholarships.name: Elks Most Valuable Student Scholarship
scholarships.eligibility: Current high school seniors who are U.S. citizens and will enroll full time in an accredited U.S. four-year undergraduate degree program. Permanent resident status alone does not qualify. No Elks family connection is required; judging considers academics, leadership, and financial need.
scholarships.expectedWindow: Open now
scholarships.whyFit: Toppenish High School qualifies geographically because this is a national scholarship for U.S. high school seniors. Individual applicants must be U.S. citizens and plan a full-time four-year degree.

scholarships.name: BigFuture Scholarship: Start Your Scholarship List (Class of 2027)
scholarships.eligibility: U.S. residents in the Class of 2027 attending school in the U.S., a U.S. territory or possession, or a DoDEA school; must have a College Board account and plan to seek an associate or bachelor's degree. Save three scholarships to earn drawing entries. No essay, GPA, or test score required.
scholarships.expectedWindow: Open now
scholarships.whyFit: Toppenish High School qualifies because the drawing accepts Class of 2027 students attending school in the U.S. Students must be U.S. residents and have a College Board account.

scholarships.name: QuestBridge National College Match
scholarships.award: Full four-year scholarships at participating partner colleges
scholarships.eligibility: High-achieving, low-income seniors currently attending high school in the U.S. and planning college the fall after graduation. QuestBridge has no absolute GPA or income cutoff, but finalists typically have very strong academics and substantial financial need.
scholarships.whyFit: Toppenish High School qualifies because the National College Match accepts any senior currently attending high school in the U.S. Individual selection remains highly competitive and based on academics, finances, and personal qualities.

scholarships.name: Ewing C. Kelly Scholarship
scholarships.eligibility: Washington high school seniors accepted to, or with an application pending at, an accredited college, community college, or technical college. U.S. citizenship or a green card is required; selection considers citizenship, achievement, activities, and financial need.
scholarships.expectedWindow: 2027 application is not released yet. The official 2026 application was postmarked by March 7; the next date may change.
scholarships.whyFit: Toppenish High School qualifies because the official application accepts high school seniors throughout Washington. Individual students must also meet the citizenship/green-card and postsecondary-application requirements.

scholarships.name: Albert Lee Wright Jr. Memorial Migrant Scholarship
scholarships.organization: National Association of State Directors of Migrant Education
scholarships.eligibility: Graduating high school seniors eligible for Title I, Part C Migrant Education who plan postsecondary education. The program especially encourages students who have overcome barriers caused by moving for agricultural or fishing work.
scholarships.expectedWindow: 2027 application is not released yet. The official 2026 deadline was March 11; use that only as a planning estimate.
scholarships.whyFit: Toppenish High School is not excluded: this is a national program for all Title I, Part C-eligible graduating seniors. Only Toppenish students who are enrolled in Migrant Education and meet the program's mobility and financial-need requirements should apply.

scholarships.name: Sea Mar Farmworker Scholarship
scholarships.eligibility: High school seniors or college students who work or have worked as farmworkers, or whose parent or guardian has; applicants must show financial need and plan full-time postsecondary enrollment.
scholarships.expectedWindow: The site is built from 2025–26 planning data. Sea Mar has offered this annually, usually January–April; confirm the 2026–27 application and deadline before applying.
scholarships.whyFit: A strong recurring option for Toppenish farmworker families. The sponsor page is currently stale, so the prior date is planning information—not a guaranteed deadline.

scholarships.name: LEAP Rise Above Scholarship
scholarships.organization: Sea Mar Community Health Centers / LEAP
scholarships.eligibility: Students who demonstrate advocacy, accountability, perseverance, and commitment to improving their community; the prior program information said citizenship status was not a barrier.
scholarships.expectedWindow: The site is built from 2025–26 planning data. This recurring program previously closed April 15; confirm the new application, rules, and deadline.
scholarships.whyFit: Toppenish students can use the prior cycle to prepare, but must confirm that the 2026–27 program and eligibility language remain the same.

scholarships.name: Sí Se Puede Scholarship
scholarships.organization: CAFÉ / Miguel R. Velazquez Migrant Education Foundation
scholarships.eligibility: Washington students connected to agricultural labor or the tree-fruit industry who demonstrate persistence, leadership, and community commitment.
scholarships.expectedWindow: The site is built from 2025–26 planning data. The program has usually run May–July; confirm the 2026–27 form and deadline.
scholarships.whyFit: Designed around Washington's agricultural and tree-fruit communities, making it especially relevant to many Toppenish families.

scholarships.name: Horatio Alger State Scholarship
scholarships.eligibility: U.S. high school seniors who show financial need, integrity, perseverance, and commitment to completing a bachelor's degree after overcoming significant adversity.
scholarships.expectedWindow: The site is built from 2025–26 planning data. This long-running program previously closed March 1; confirm the current state-scholarship cycle.
scholarships.whyFit: Toppenish students are geographically eligible for the state program when they meet the sponsor's financial, academic, citizenship, and degree-plan requirements.

scholarships.name: McDonald's HACER National Scholarship
scholarships.eligibility: High school seniors with at least one parent of Hispanic heritage who meet the sponsor's GPA, residency, and college-enrollment requirements.
scholarships.expectedWindow: The site is built from 2025–26 planning data. The prior deadline was February 17; confirm the 2026–27 opening and rules.
scholarships.whyFit: A recurring national opportunity relevant to many Toppenish students with Hispanic family heritage.

scholarships.name: Washington State Governors' Scholarship for Foster Youth
scholarships.eligibility: Washington high school seniors who have experienced qualifying foster care and plan to enroll in an eligible college or training program.
scholarships.expectedWindow: The site is built from 2025–26 planning data. The prior deadline was January 30; confirm the 2026–27 application and foster-care eligibility rules.
scholarships.whyFit: Toppenish students with qualifying foster-care experience can plan ahead using the prior cycle, then confirm the current requirements privately with counseling.

scholarships.name: NAEHCY Scholarship Fund
scholarships.organization: National Association for the Education of Homeless Children and Youth
scholarships.award: Up to $3,000 in the prior cycle
scholarships.eligibility: Students pursuing postsecondary education who have experienced homelessness and meet the sponsor's current documentation and application requirements.
scholarships.expectedWindow: The site is built from 2025–26 planning data. The prior deadline was July 31; confirm whether and when the next scholarship cycle opens.
scholarships.whyFit: Toppenish students are not excluded, but this is sensitive eligibility. Students should ask counseling privately for help confirming documentation.

scholarships.name: SchoolHouse Connection Youth Leadership and Scholarship Program
scholarships.award: $2,000 in the prior cycle plus support
scholarships.eligibility: Students who have experienced homelessness and are entering or continuing postsecondary education; prior information included undocumented students who met the program criteria.
scholarships.expectedWindow: The site is built from 2025–26 planning resources using the last available June 2 date. Confirm that the program, amount, and current deadline have returned.
scholarships.whyFit: A potentially valuable recurring program for students who have experienced housing instability; confirm eligibility privately with a trusted adult.

scholarships.name: Truman D. Picard Scholarship
scholarships.eligibility: Native American students pursuing higher education in natural resources or related fields who meet the sponsor's tribal-documentation and enrollment rules.
scholarships.expectedWindow: The site is built from 2025–26 planning data. The prior deadline was March 20; confirm the next cycle, award, and documentation requirements.
scholarships.whyFit: Especially relevant for Yakama and other Native students interested in forestry, natural resources, or related careers.

scholarships.name: AISES Scholarships for Indigenous Students in STEM
scholarships.organization: American Indian Science and Engineering Society
scholarships.eligibility: Eligible Indigenous students pursuing STEM who meet the current scholarship's membership, enrollment, and tribal or Indigenous documentation rules.
scholarships.expectedWindow: The site is built from 2025–26 planning data. The prior deadline was April 30; individual AISES awards may use different dates, so confirm the current listing.
scholarships.whyFit: A strong recurring group of opportunities for Yakama and other Indigenous students entering STEM fields.

scholarships.name: Indian Health Service Scholarships
scholarships.award: Tuition and other support varies by program
scholarships.eligibility: American Indian and Alaska Native students entering eligible health-profession programs who meet the current citizenship, tribal, enrollment, and service-obligation rules.
scholarships.expectedWindow: The site is built from 2025–26 planning data. The prior deadline was February 28; confirm the next cycle and service obligations before applying.
scholarships.whyFit: Potentially significant support for Yakama and other Native students pursuing eligible health careers; requirements differ by IHS program.

scholarships.name: Microsoft Disability Scholarship
scholarships.award: Up to $20,000 in the prior program information
scholarships.eligibility: High school seniors with a disability who plan eligible undergraduate study and meet the current academic, financial-need, and technology-related interest requirements.
scholarships.expectedWindow: The site is built from 2025–26 planning data. The prior deadline was March 16; confirm the current sponsor page, eligible majors, and application date.
scholarships.whyFit: Toppenish students with disabilities can plan ahead, but the current cycle and eligible field requirements must be confirmed.

scholarships.name: INCIGHT Scholarship
scholarships.eligibility: Students with disabilities pursuing higher education who demonstrate community involvement, perseverance, and leadership.
scholarships.expectedWindow: The site is built from 2025–26 planning data. The prior deadline was April 15; confirm the next cycle and disability documentation rules.
scholarships.whyFit: A recurring regional opportunity for Toppenish students with disabilities who are involved in their community.

scholarships.name: Pride Foundation Scholarship
scholarships.eligibility: LGBTQIA+ students and allies from Washington and other eligible Northwest states who meet the current program's education and community criteria.
scholarships.expectedWindow: The site is built from 2025–26 planning data. The prior deadline was January 9; confirm the current application window and award criteria.
scholarships.whyFit: A recurring Northwest scholarship program open to eligible Toppenish students; use disclosure-safe filters on shared devices.

scholarships.name: GSBA Scholarship Fund
scholarships.eligibility: Washington LGBTQIA+ students and allies who demonstrate leadership, academic ability, and involvement in school or community.
scholarships.expectedWindow: The site is built from 2025–26 planning data. The prior deadline was January 10; confirm the current award levels and application window.
scholarships.whyFit: A Washington-focused recurring opportunity that eligible Toppenish students may overlook.

scholarships.name: Burger King Scholars
scholarships.eligibility: High school seniors meeting the current GPA and residency rules who plan full-time enrollment in college or vocational school; selection can consider work, service, activities, and financial need.
scholarships.expectedWindow: The site is built from 2025–26 planning data. The last available deadline was December 15; confirm the current cycle before applying.
scholarships.whyFit: Broad recurring award that includes vocational programs and values work experience—relevant to many Toppenish students.

scholarships.name: American Legion Oratorical Contest
scholarships.award: Washington awards totaled $5,000 in the prior cycle, plus possible national awards
scholarships.eligibility: Students in grades 9–12 who are eligible under the current contest rules and are willing to deliver a prepared and assigned speech about the U.S. Constitution; no veteran-parent connection is required.
scholarships.expectedWindow: The site is built from 2025–26 planning data. Local and state rounds occur before the national contest; contact the Washington sponsor to confirm the 2026–27 entry deadline.
scholarships.whyFit: Worth considering for strong Toppenish speakers and writers. The prior date is for planning and is not guaranteed.

scholarships.name: Jack Kent Cooke College Scholarship Program
scholarships.award: Up to $55,000 per year; amount varies by student need and aid
scholarships.eligibility: High-achieving high school seniors with financial need who plan to enroll full time in an accredited four-year undergraduate program. Review the sponsor's current GPA, financial-need, citizenship/residency, and college rules before applying.
scholarships.expectedWindow: 2026 application period: August 19–November 11
scholarships.whyFit: Toppenish students qualify geographically because this is a national scholarship. A student still needs the sponsor's high-achievement, financial-need, and college-enrollment qualifications.
scholarships.needs: Application, transcript and course information, financial-aid information, and the sponsor's required writing or supporting materials.

scholarships.name: American Indian College Fund Full Circle Scholarship
scholarships.award: Multiple scholarship opportunities through one application; awards vary
scholarships.eligibility: Native American or Alaska Native students who can document tribal enrollment or descendancy, have at least a 2.0 GPA, and plan full-time enrollment at a nonprofit accredited college or university.
scholarships.expectedWindow: Applications open every February 1; priority review deadline is May 31. Dates and requirements can change.
scholarships.whyFit: Toppenish students with qualifying Native affiliation can apply nationally, including students planning a nonprofit community college, university, or other eligible program.
scholarships.needs: Online application, transcript, photo, tribal enrollment or descendancy documentation, and three short-answer responses.

scholarships.name: Native Forward Scholars Fund
scholarships.award: Multiple awards; amounts vary by program
scholarships.eligibility: Eligible American Indian or Alaska Native students enrolled full time in a degree-seeking program at an accredited U.S. institution who can provide tribal eligibility documentation and meet the current financial-need rules.
scholarships.expectedWindow: Planning estimate: May 2027 opening based on the annual July 15 document deadline. The Financial Needs Form and Tribal Eligibility Certificate are due July 15 each academic year; confirm the new cycle before applying.
scholarships.whyFit: A Toppenish student with qualifying tribal affiliation may be eligible nationwide. The student must verify the current program, enrollment, FAFSA, tribal-documentation, and financial-need requirements.
scholarships.needs: FAFSA, Financial Needs Form, Tribal Eligibility Certificate, enrollment information, transcript, and any program-specific documents.
